reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

description.narrative:
Over the reporting the program created more opportunities for youth to participate in civic and governance issues by helping them organize forums that involved 480 participants (310 men, 170 women, including 8 people with disabilities). It used social media to educate youth and promote accountability through weekly posts, a ‘board of fame’ for good leadership, and a ‘board of shame’ for poor performance.
Youth organizations were supported to carry out advocacy based on local governance issues. This led to the creation of the "Office of the Citizen," where youth could raise concerns—17 cases are currently being handled. Their efforts resulted in better services, like improved waste collection and restarting of stalled projects. Youth also learned how to write official letters, submitting three to the county. Technology helped connect youth to leaders through new social media platforms in Homa Bay, Kericho, and Busia. One result was government funding for a school toilet in Awuoro primary school.
Overall, the program increased youth awareness of democracy, law, and inclusive politics. Young people are now actively identifying problems and advocating for change. County-based organizations improved their ability to raise issues through letters, petitions, and campaigns, leading to actions like waste bin installations and resumption of paused projects. A new CBO partner, Maria Rusanna CBO, joined to help sustain the program’s impact.
